label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Kavya, I'm tagging you here because you deserve to hear this from me directly, not through 60 comments.

Some of you have seen the post about founders DMing their batchmates' teams with 40% hikes. That was about me, and I won't pretend otherwise. Two people from our Foundry91 cohort 4 joined DabbaDost this month. Here's what actually happened, and where I got it wrong.

On 14 September we posted a backend developer opening on our LinkedIn page and on Instahyre. It was open to anyone. The first candidate applied on his own on 19 September. The second came in as his referral about two weeks later. Nobody from my side reached out to anyone at SitterNest. I didn't DM anyone.

The offer was 22% over current CTC, not 40%. Both joined on 3 November. If you've been repeating the 40% number, please update it.

Here's my mistake. I knew where both of them worked from day one. I should have called Kavya before making the offers, not after. That's on me. It was a basic courtesy between two founders in the same batch, and I skipped it.

Some of what was said also isn't accurate. We did not promise ESOPs we don't have. We have an option pool. It's small, but it's real, and it's been on paper since January.

Kavya, you sat with me until 1am in the Koramangala office fixing our Razorpay webhook mess before demo day. I've never forgotten that, and I respect you deeply, as a founder and as a friend. I sent you a WhatsApp after the second offer was accepted, and you didn't reply. I understand why. I should have handled this much better.

This isn't a fight, and I don't want it to become one. We're eleven startups in this batch, all hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will keep happening unless we agree on how to handle it.

So here's a simple rule I'd like us to adopt: if you're interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before you make an offer. One message. That's it.

Kavya, coffee or a call, whenever you're comfortable. I'm open this week, so just tell me a time.

---

Notes before you post:
- It's about 410 words and roughly 2,500 characters, so it fits both limits.
- Check that you're okay sharing the ESOP pool detail publicly. If the pool terms are confidential, cut that paragraph.
- The 1am line is the most personal part. Keep it if you want the post to show respect, and cut it if it feels like too much in front of the batch.
- The two engineers aren't named anywhere.
